- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.6) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — delay downward adjustment by 1–2 periods.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), reduce subsequent forecast by 3–5% to account for mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.2–0.6) and forecast deviates >3% from true, apply a smoothing filter to reduce volatility bias.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early mean reversion (first 5–7 days), adjust forecast downward by 1–2% to align with sentiment-driven correction.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated reversal patterns (e.g., +0.6 → -0.4 → +0.6), model should lag 1–2 periods to avoid sentiment overfitting.
